personas.name: June, the Ratel
personas.who: A mother in her forties who never thought of herself as a gamer. She found the Ratel's hex puzzle in the Toybox when her son left the game open, and plays it as a casual puzzle game in short gaps. Her son keeps asking her to join his squad.
personas.challenge: Her bridge is the crew seat, and today it has gaps. The Honeyguide seats no arena card (fleet/Honeyguide.yaml arenas: []), so the son cannot bring her to his arena nights, only to a Mass-Space game or a voyage. A voyage cell runs 45 to 180 s but a voyage runs 20 to 40 min, past her 10 minute gaps, so she needs a voyage that can be left after any cell and picked up later. Activation for her is a shot she made landing, not the Lesson's first combo: the Mentor never teaches the board.

stages.name: The Ratel puzzle on its own
stages.note: She sits in the Ratel's seat while the Honeyguide's AI flies, and plays the Dynamo board for patterns. She never touches the flight controls.
stages.milestone: Four patterns in one sitting, and an ability picked
stages.why: her son sends a party invite

personas.name: The Night Shift
personas.who: Four friends in their twenties who hit the arena most nights on voice chat, and binge voyages on the weekend.
personas.challenge: Their nights live or die on the arena's balance: one dominant hull and they all fly it, the squad book goes flat, and they leave by week four. That is the arena balancing project's plateau work, and the gene search's style check (does a balance change collapse a vessel to one behaviour) is the early warning. Their weekend binge is the only persona that finishes voyages as they are built today.

personas.name: Aiko, the commuter racer
personas.who: Late twenties, plays one-handed on the train twice a day, sound off. Races the Time games and climbs the rung ladder; has never opened the arena.
personas.challenge: Challenge to the plan: she may never want the arena. Regatta is her natural door (every Time game is training for Regatta), but a 10 to 25 minute ride fits one arena round, not an arena set. A single Regatta race against the trained Time AIs, as a ladder rung, would let the balance work reach her.

cultures.name: Snack sessions
cultures.is: Short gaps in a day (a queue, a coffee, the couch before dinner). Common in casual mobile play everywhere.

cultures.name: Commute slots
cultures.is: Two fixed rides a day, ten to thirty minutes, one hand, often no sound. The pattern is strongest where most people ride trains to work (Tokyo, Seoul, Shanghai, London are examples of where it is common, not of who plays).

cultures.name: Evening sit-down
cultures.is: One long sitting after work or school, at a PC or console or on a couch with a phone, sound on, often with friends in a voice channel.

cultures.name: Weekend binge
cultures.is: Little on weekdays, long runs on Saturday and Sunday. Common among students and shift workers, and in PC-cafe play where a group books hours together.
